meta.headline: Defense is being re-platformed around autonomy, software and industrial capacity, and the money has already moved.

forces.t: Autonomy gets its own budget and command
forces.b: The FY27 request moves the Defense Autonomous Warfare Group from $225M to $54.6B and Drone Dominance to $53.6B. Hegseth ordered a four-star Autonomous Warfare Command to stand up by Oct 2027. Unmanned systems are becoming a budget category of their own, not an add-on.

forces.t: Software and AI take control of the kill chain
forces.b: Maven is becoming the DoD standard; Scale AI's CDAO deal is now $500M; frontier labs (Anthropic, OpenAI, Google, xAI) run on classified networks. Value moves to the layer that fuses data and chooses targets.
$2–5k attack drones, lasers firing for under $5 a shot, and a CCA under $20M, set against interceptors costing millions. Buyers now judge every system by what each engagement costs.

forces.t: Rebuilding the industrial base is the new moat
forces.b: New factories (Anduril's Arsenal-1 and Arsenal-2, Hadrian at $7.9B, Castelion's Project Ranger), rare-earth independence (MP Materials, the Jan 2027 magnet ban) and on-base nuclear power (Janus, $2.2B). Whoever can produce at volume wins.

Golden Dome ($185B official estimate; $1.2T per CBO), SpaceX's $6.45B in space-layer awards, SDA constellations, and GEO surveillance (GHOST-R). Most new sensing and communications architecture now runs through orbit.

forces.t: Allies' wars are the test range
forces.b: Ukraine expects about 4.5M FPV drones in 2026 and fields 25,000 ground robots; Israel used lasers in the 2026 Iran war; Taiwan passed a $7.6B drone industry act; Europe is spending €454B. Combat-proven products sell first.

forces.t: Capital is plentiful, but exits are the test
forces.b: $40.8B of VC in H1 2026, IPOs (York Space, an Ursa Major SPAC), and the primes at record backlogs (Lockheed $230B, RTX $289B). Incumbents are not dying; they are buying and teaming.

forces.t: Political and funding risk is real
forces.b: FY27 opened on a stopgap that runs to 11 Dec. Golden Dome's lead warns of funding jeopardy. Access is concentrated in a few politically connected firms. Treat budget lines as unconfirmed until appropriated.

briefs.title: The money is moving to cheap, smart and made-at-home
briefs.big: The Pentagon is shifting from a few expensive weapons to many cheap drones, the software that runs them, and the factories that build them. The next two months decide how much of that money actually arrives.

stories.h: Anduril is building a shipyard for Navy submarine parts
stories.what: The defense startup announced a giant new yard in Maryland to make submarine parts, an area the old defense giants have owned for decades.
stories.you: Startups aren't only writing software anymore; they're building heavy industry. Making things at scale is now a real way into defense.

stories.h: The Pentagon wants a dedicated command for drones and robots
stories.what: Defense Secretary Hegseth ordered a new top-level military command just for autonomous systems, with its own budget. Congress still has to approve it.
stories.you: Anyone building drones, robots or autonomy software would get one big, dedicated customer. Watch whether Congress backs it.

stories.h: Lasers that shoot down drones are going into mass production
stories.what: The Army signed its first-ever production deal for a laser weapon. Each shot costs a few dollars, compared with missiles that cost a fortune.
stories.you: Stopping cheap drones cheaply is the industry's hottest problem. Anything that makes it cheaper, faster or easier to deploy has buyers.

stories.h: China is squeezing the magnets every drone needs
stories.what: China is tightening exports of rare-earth magnets just as the Pentagon prepares to ban Chinese magnets from its supply chain in January.
stories.you: Supply chains are now a weapon. Tools or parts that help companies source compliant components will be needed fast.

stories.h: Musk and Palmer Luckey are helping plan the future of war
stories.what: The Pentagon asked Elon Musk and Anduril's founder to lead a four-month study of what the military should build next. Their report lands in late January.
stories.you: That report is a preview of where defense spending goes next. Read it the day it comes out.

watch.h: Congress has until December 11 to fund the Pentagon
watch.why: The military is running on a temporary budget. Until Congress passes the real one, the big new drone and missile-defense money is only a promise.

idea.h: A parts-sourcing checker for drone makers
idea.why: Software that tells a drone company which of its parts break the new magnet rules, and where to buy compliant replacements. Hundreds of hardware startups need it before January.

sectors.name: AI, software & command and control
sectors.state: Command-and-control and decision software is the most valuable layer in defense. Palantir's Maven is moving to a DoD-wide program of record, and NATO also uses it. CDAO has raised Scale AI's deal to $500M and given frontier-model contracts (up to $200M each) to Anthropic, OpenAI, Google and xAI for classified use. Delivery tooling for air-gapped networks is also getting funded: Defense Unicorns won up to $350M.
sectors.money: CDAO enterprise deals; Army Enterprise Agreement ($10B Palantir); a share of DAWG for autonomy software
sectors.watch: Open-architecture and data-rights rules that could commoditize the layer; agentic AI moving onto IL6/IL7 networks; Palantir Q3 results (early Nov).

sectors.name: Drones & air autonomy
sectors.state: Two markets at once. Cheap mass: Drone Dominance aims for 200k+ small attack drones by 2027 at $5k falling to $2.3k, and Neros has a $500M Army FPV IDIQ. High end: CCA, where Anduril's FQ-44A and GA's YFQ-42 are in production, Increment 2 has 9 vendors in concept work, and Navy CCA Increment 1 is starting. Shield AI's X-BAT is drawing Navy interest.
sectors.money: $39.2B FY27 request for autonomous systems procurement; CCA lines; Army PBAS
sectors.watch: Unit prices in later gauntlets; CCA Inc 2 downselect to about 6 vendors; Navy carrier CCA award.

sectors.name: Maritime & undersea autonomy
sectors.state: Cheap autonomous surface vessels and large undersea drones are the Navy's answer to its shipbuilding crisis. Saronic ($9.25B) and Blue Water Autonomy are building their own yards. HavocAI is in Navy MUSV at-sea testing and partnered with Hanwha. Blue Water and Saildrone are suing the Navy over the MUSV rejection. Anduril's Arsenal-2 brings startups into Virginia-class submarine parts.
sectors.money: MUSV (~$6B production ambition); submarine industrial base money; Taiwan's 1,000-USV plan
sectors.watch: MUSV litigation; first Blue Water hull launch; Taiwan coastal-denial buys.

sectors.name: Ground robotics
sectors.state: Ukraine runs about 10,000 robot logistics missions a month and plans 25,000 ground robots. The US is slower and still years from large-scale autonomous ground operations, but contracts are flowing: Overland AI ($24.5M with Rangers, $20M autonomous breaching), Forterra and Scout AI, and six vendors in Infantry Last Tactical Mile.
sectors.money: Army Transformation Initiative; small OTAs; ATI/APFIT
sectors.watch: Whether the Army turns prototypes into a program of record by 2028.

sectors.name: Space
sectors.state: SpaceX dominates the military space layers: $2.29B for the MILNET-based Space Data Network backbone and $4.16B for SB-AMTI. SDA continues its tranche buys. True Anomaly won GHOST-R GEO surveillance satellites and space-based interceptor work. York Space is public and acquiring; Apex and K2 are scaling satellite buses.
sectors.money: Space Force; SDA tranches; Golden Dome space layer
sectors.watch: Concentration on SpaceX; launch cadence of T2 Transport Layer; space-control (offensive and defensive) budgets.

sectors.name: Missile defense & Golden Dome
sectors.state: Golden Dome is the decade's biggest new program: $185B official estimate through 2035, $1.2T over 20 years per CBO. Twelve firms are prototyping space-based interceptors for a 2028 demonstration. Anduril and Palantir reportedly lead the command software. Gen. Guetlein warns FY27 funding uncertainty could put it at risk. Lockheed's $35B THAAD multiyear shows the primes still own the interceptors.
sectors.money: $24.4B from the 2025 reconciliation law plus annual appropriations
sectors.watch: FY27 appropriations by 11 Dec; formal C2 awards; first SBI tests.

sectors.name: Missiles, hypersonics & munitions
sectors.state: Munitions shortages (see CNAS) are pulling startups into solid rocket motors and low-cost strike. Castelion signed a Blackbeard production deal and is building a plant for 500+ a year in New Mexico. Ursa Major is going public in a $2.3B deal and won $137M from the Navy for rocket motors. Anduril partnered with Voyager on propulsion. HACM flew with Australia.
sectors.money: Munitions multiyear procurement; Navy SM motor second sources; hypersonic RDT&E
sectors.watch: Second-source rocket motor awards; Castelion test results; Ursa Major listing.

sectors.name: Counter-drone & directed energy
sectors.state: The mirror image of the drone boom, with $14.4B requested for FY27. AeroVironment won the first-ever US production contract for a high-energy laser ($464.8M, LOCUST, under $5 a shot). Epirus's microwave weapon beat a fiber-optic drone and is the only one in DoD's base-defense pilot. Interceptor drones are spreading from Ukraine to Japan and the Gulf. CHAOS ($4.5B) is building the radar.
sectors.money: FY27 counter-UAS ($14.4B); Replicator 2; base-defense pilot
sectors.watch: Domestic counter-drone legal authority; interceptor-drone programs of record; Israel Iron Beam fielding.

sectors.name: Electronic warfare & spectrum
sectors.state: Software-defined EW and spectrum sensing are being bought fast. The Army made its first production awards under an EW call for solutions: Heaviside $99M (MOTH) and Research Innovations $96.9M (Dragonfly). Fiber-optic drones bypass jamming, so the sector is shifting toward sensing and attribution. L3Harris holds the large legacy jammer programs.
sectors.money: Army EW call for solutions; FY27 Army EW boost
sectors.watch: EW for small units; anti-jam datalinks for swarms.

sectors.name: Cyber & information
sectors.state: Chinese state actors (Salt Typhoon) remain inside telecom and government networks, per the FBI. Offensive cyber startups raise early rounds (RemoteThreat, $7M pre-seed). Defense cyber gets less venture money than hardware, a possible gap. Air-gapped software delivery (Defense Unicorns) shows that 'cyber' increasingly means secure deployment.
sectors.money: CYBERCOM budgets; CDAO; service cyber lines
sectors.watch: New Salt Typhoon disclosures; offensive cyber authorities.

sectors.name: Sensing, ISR & quantum
sectors.state: GPS-denied navigation is the most funded use of quantum sensing. Q-CTRL has DARPA RoQS awards (~US$24M) and a DIU contract with Lockheed. SandboxAQ's AQNav is in DIU's quantum-sensing transition program. DARPA moved more firms into Stage C of its Quantum Benchmarking Initiative. DIU is running a prize fly-off for low-cost ISR.
sectors.money: DIU TQS; DARPA RoQS and QBI
sectors.watch: First quantum navigation programs of record; low-cost ISR fly-off winners.

sectors.name: Manufacturing & industrial base
sectors.state: Factories are now a venture category. Hadrian raised $1.37B at $7.87B, Divergent builds additively, and Firestorm makes drones in hours. Anduril has Arsenal-1 (Fury) and Arsenal-2 ($6.6B submarine yard). Neros targets 1M drones a year by 2028. The Office of Strategic Capital is lending to domestic supply chains.
sectors.money: OSC loans; Defense Production Act Title III; Navy submarine industrial base funds
sectors.watch: Factory output against promises; labor; OSC deal flow.

sectors.name: Critical minerals & supply chain
sectors.state: China refines about 91% of rare earths and controls almost all heavy rare-earth processing. In June 2026 Beijing put MP Materials and USA Rare Earth on its export-control list. DoD holds a stake in MP, with a 10-year offtake deal and a $110/kg price floor. DoD bans Chinese, Russian, Iranian and North Korean magnets from 1 Jan 2027, and dysprosium and terbium remain the gap.
sectors.money: DoD equity and offtake deals; DPA Title III; OSC
sectors.watch: China's 10 Nov magnet deadline; heavy rare-earth separation outside China; drone motors that use no magnets.

sectors.name: Energy & nuclear power
sectors.state: Bases need resilient power for AI, sensors and directed energy. The Army's Janus program picked five microreactor developers ($2.2B): Antares, BWXT, GA-EMS, Radiant and Westinghouse. Project Pele's TRISO fuel has arrived. Valar Atomics' reactor was airlifted by C-17s. Radiant has a deal for 15 Kaleidos units.
sectors.money: Army Janus; DIU/SCO Pele; DOE
sectors.watch: First reactor operating on a base; tactical power for lasers.

sectors.name: Biotech & biomanufacturing
sectors.state: Quieter but strategic. DoD's Distributed Bioindustrial Manufacturing Program made 34 awards ($60.2M) for domestic bio-production of fuels, materials and chemicals to reduce reliance on adversaries. Biosecurity and bio-based munitions precursors are emerging venture themes.
sectors.money: DBIMP; DTRA; BARDA (adjacent)
sectors.watch: DBIMP phase-two scale-up awards; biosecurity in the next NDAA.

sectors.name: Budget, policy & acquisition reform
sectors.state: The FY26 NDAA wrote the SPEED and FoRGED reforms into law: Portfolio Acquisition Executives and preference for commercial products. The FY27 request is about $1.5T with record autonomy lines, but FY27 opened under a stopgap that runs to 11 Dec. Hegseth ordered an Autonomous Warfare Command and an interim team (Project Agincourt) for 'warfighting acquisition'. Project Meridian (Musk, Luckey, Gingrich) reports in late Jan 2027.
sectors.money: FY27 appropriations; reconciliation; DAWG
sectors.watch: 11 Dec funding deadline; NDAA conference on a robotics combatant command; Meridian report.

sectors.name: Capital: VC, M&A & IPOs
sectors.state: Record $40.8B of VC in H1 2026 (PitchBook) and $69.5B over the last 12 months. Money is a barbell: mega-rounds and seed rounds, with mid-stage squeezed. 2026 megarounds include Anduril $5B, Helsing, Shield AI $1.5B, Hadrian $1.37B, Saronic $1.75B and Quantum Systems €1B. Exits are reopening: York Space IPO, Ursa Major SPAC, Karman roll-ups.
sectors.money: Growth equity, private credit (Blackstone), bank strategic funds (JPMorgan)
sectors.watch: Anduril S-1; down rounds for gauntlet losers; primes buying startups.

sectors.name: Incumbent primes
sectors.state: The primes are not losing. They post record backlogs (Lockheed $230B, RTX $289B) and raised guidance on missiles and missile defense (PAC-3, THAAD, PrSM). Their strategy is to partner (Lockheed with Q-CTRL, GA in CCA), build CCA variants (Northrop YFQ-48A), and buy companies. Their soft spots are software, speed and cheap mass.
sectors.money: Multiyear munitions; missile defense; F-35/B-21 sustainment
sectors.watch: Prime acquisitions of startups; who loses share in CCA Inc 2 and Golden Dome C2.

sectors.name: Allies & theaters
sectors.state: Ukraine expects about 4.5M FPV drones in 2026 (8–10M capacity), 590k drone orders on Brave1 in nine months, and is exporting its model. Israel used lasers in the 2026 Iran war and has 600+ defense startups. Europe: €454B in 2026, the €150B SAFE loan fund, and NATO's 5% target. Indo-Pacific: Taiwan's $7.6B drone act, Japan's interceptor-drone buy, and AUKUS swarm trials.
sectors.money: EU SAFE; national budgets; FMS; Ukraine aid and co-production
sectors.watch: Ukrainian co-production in the EU and US; Taiwan's budget politics; Gulf counter-drone demand.

sectors.name: Adversaries: China, Russia, Iran
sectors.state: The PLA has demonstrated one operator controlling 200+ drones (the Atlas system), unmanned stealth designs, and layered counter-drone defenses with lasers and microwaves. Russia is building a sovereign drone ecosystem (CSIS). China is using rare-earth export controls as a weapon. Iranian drones and missiles shaped the 2026 Israel and Gulf air-defense lessons.
sectors.money: Drives US requirements: threat-based budgeting
sectors.watch: PLA exercises around Taiwan; new export controls; Russia–Iran drone cooperation.

updates.title: Army awards Defense Unicorns up to $350M for its air-gapped Unified Defense Stack
updates.body: An indefinite-delivery contract for software that ships and runs applications on disconnected, classified and edge networks.
updates.why: Getting software onto air-gapped networks is a bottleneck for every AI vendor. The company that controls deployment becomes infrastructure.

updates.title: DARPA moves four more quantum computing companies into Stage C of its benchmarking initiative
updates.body: That brings the Stage C group to six, the stage where independent evaluators judge whether utility-scale machines can be built.
updates.why: A government-validated quantum shortlist shapes which firms get national-security work.

updates.title: Navy awards Ursa Major $137M for solid rocket motors on two missile programs
updates.body: Part of the push to add domestic second sources for missile propulsion.
updates.why: Rocket motors are the munitions bottleneck. Startups are breaking the two-supplier duopoly.

updates.title: Overland AI gets $4.5M more to field autonomous vehicles with the 75th Ranger Regiment
updates.body: Its total under the APFIT program is now $24.5M.
updates.why: Elite units are the first users of ground autonomy. That is how programs of record start.

updates.title: Goldman upgrades Palantir to Buy ($230 target); Karp says an exec told him to stop hyping Foundry
updates.body: PLTR rose 3.2% while the market fell. Barclays started coverage at Overweight.
updates.why: Commercial AI momentum is now holding up the defense software leader's valuation.

updates.title: Anduril and Navy announce the $6.6B Arsenal-2 submarine-component shipyard in Maryland
updates.body: Anduril invests $3.7B in a 2M sq ft yard at Sparrows Point. A Navy contract worth up to $2.9B, paid per unit produced, covers Virginia-class parts such as torpedo tubes and doors. Operations start in 2030, with 3,100 direct jobs.
updates.why: A venture-backed company is entering heavy shipbuilding, the primes' most protected territory.

updates.title: US Air Force and Australia flight-test the Hypersonic Attack Cruise Missile
updates.body: A joint flight test under the US–Australia hypersonics partnership.
updates.why: Hypersonics move toward fielding. Allied co-development (AUKUS) is now the norm.

updates.title: Navy adds $150M of export-ready engineering to Shield AI's X-BAT before its first flight
updates.body: Money to design the aircraft for foreign sales from the start.
updates.why: Autonomous jets are being designed for allied markets from day one. Exports are a growth path.

updates.title: China's 10 Nov magnet deadline collides with DoD's 1 Jan 2027 ban on Chinese magnets
updates.body: Defense suppliers face a squeeze: Beijing is tightening export licensing while the Pentagon bars rare-earth magnets from adversary nations starting 1 January.
updates.why: Every motor, actuator and seeker depends on these magnets. Supply gaps hit drones and munitions first.

updates.title: FY27 opens on a stopgap: the Pentagon is funded at FY26 levels until 11 Dec
updates.body: The continuing resolution passed the Senate 90–6 and the House 370–48. New starts, including DAWG's huge increase, wait for full-year appropriations.
updates.why: Programs that depend on new FY27 money (DAWG, Golden Dome growth) slip until Congress acts.

updates.title: Project Meridian: Musk, Luckey and Gingrich lead a 120-day Pentagon study of future warfare
updates.body: Under CTO Emil Michael, with MITRE managing conflicts of interest. Scope covers AI, robotics, autonomous weapons, directed energy and biotech, from underground to cislunar space. The report is due late January 2027.
updates.why: The founders of the biggest new defense companies are helping set requirements. Read the report when it lands.

updates.title: Epirus Leonidas is the only microwave weapon in DoD's pilot to defend US installations
updates.body: It is also wired into the Army's layered counter-drone network.
updates.why: Defending US bases against drones is now a funded mission.

updates.title: Palantir partners with Armada on sovereign AI infrastructure
updates.body: Palantir software on rugged edge data centers that the customer owns.
updates.why: The software leader is moving into deployable compute for countries that need AI inside their own borders.

updates.title: Hegseth orders a four-star Autonomous Warfare Command and an interim team, Project Agincourt
updates.body: The command would have service-like powers, its own budget and new career fields, with a target of Oct 2027. Agincourt will prototype 'warfighting acquisition'. Congress must act; the SASC bill proposes a robotics combatant command.
updates.why: Drones get a dedicated buyer with its own money: the main future customer for autonomy firms.

updates.title: Anduril and Voyager partner on advanced weapons and propulsion
updates.body: Development, test, qualification and high-rate production for weapons and missile defense.
updates.why: Propulsion is a munitions chokepoint. New entrants are securing supply.

updates.title: Ukrainian troops ordered 590,000+ drones on the Brave1 Market in nine months
updates.body: Ukraine expects about 4.5M FPV drones in 2026 from about 500 makers, with capacity for 8–10M.
updates.why: The volume benchmark that everyone else's drone programs are measured against.

updates.title: Tekever raises $580M at a $6.4B valuation
updates.body: The Portuguese ISR-drone maker's Series D was led by UC Investments and Baillie Gifford.
updates.why: Europe's drone tier is reaching decacorn scale.

updates.title: Northrop and True Anomaly win GHOST-R satellites to inspect objects in geostationary orbit
updates.body: Space Systems Command and DIU prototypes for high-resolution reconnaissance of other satellites.
updates.why: Space control is becoming a budget line, and a startup is sharing it with a prime.

updates.title: Army awards Palantir and Anduril $192M to produce TITAN
updates.body: TITAN, the next-generation mobile intelligence ground station, moves into production.
updates.why: The two new leaders win more as a team than as rivals.

updates.title: Fury officially designated FQ-44A; unit cost said to be well below $20M
updates.body: The Air Force aims for 500 combat-ready CCAs by 2032.
updates.why: A startup-built combat jet at roughly a fifth of a fighter's cost.

updates.title: Army makes its first EW production awards: Heaviside $99M and Research Innovations $96.9M
updates.body: MOTH spectrum analyzers and AI-driven Dragonfly sensors, under a rapid call for solutions.
updates.why: Shows how fast commercial-style contracting can move startups from call to production.

updates.title: Overland AI wins $20M for autonomous minefield breaching
updates.body: One of four companies (with Caterpillar, Forterra and IDV) in the Army's Engineer Autonomous Breaching Capability.
updates.why: Dangerous, repetitive jobs are where ground autonomy gets bought first.

updates.title: Boeing and Anduril downselected for the IFPC Inc 2 second interceptor
updates.body: Both advance in the Army's competition for a cruise-missile and drone defense interceptor.
updates.why: A new entrant competes head-to-head with a prime for interceptor money.

updates.title: AeroVironment wins $464.8M for the first-ever US production contract for a high-energy laser
updates.body: Dozens of 30kW LOCUST X3 lasers for the Army's Enduring-High Energy Laser program, mounted on JLTVs or pallets. Under $5 per shot against Group 1–3 drones.
updates.why: Lasers have moved from demonstrations to production, changing the cost of defending against drones.

updates.title: Navy starts its search for carrier-based CCA Increment 1
updates.body: NAVAIR wants two autonomous prototypes flying within 24 months and certified for shore-based carrier operations within three years.
updates.why: A second large CCA buyer is coming, open to new entrants.

updates.title: Army picks five firms for $2.2B on-base microreactor program (Janus)
updates.body: Antares (Fort Bragg), BWXT (Fort Campbell), GA-EMS (Fort Hood), Radiant (Fort Benning) and Westinghouse (Fort Drum).
updates.why: Bases need resilient power for AI, sensors and lasers. Nuclear startups now have a defense customer.

updates.title: First White House 'Drone Dominance' meeting with about 100 companies
updates.body: The $1.1B program aims for 200,000+ small lethal drones by 2027 through four production 'gauntlets'. Phase one: 12 vendors and 30,000 one-way attack drones at about $5k each, falling toward $2.3k.
updates.why: The government is setting the price for mass-produced drones.

updates.title: Ursa Major to go public in a $2.3B deal
updates.body: The hypersonics and solid-rocket-motor maker is listing.
updates.why: Exits for hard-tech defense companies are reopening.

updates.title: Army awards six prototype contracts for Infantry Last Tactical Mile ground robots
updates.body: Unmanned vehicles for logistics and casualty evacuation; Overland AI and Forterra are among the six.
updates.why: The ground-robot market is forming around logistics first, as it did in Ukraine.

updates.title: Taiwan passes a NT$240B ($7.6B) six-year act for drones and uncrewed systems
updates.body: Taiwan plans 200,000+ UAVs and 1,000 USVs from domestic, non-Chinese supply chains, and has reclassified drones as consumables.
updates.why: A large new buyer of drones and parts free of Chinese supply chains, including from US and Japanese partners.

updates.title: Guetlein: Golden Dome is in jeopardy because of FY27 funding uncertainty
updates.body: The program manager warns that stopgap funding threatens the schedule.
updates.why: Even the top priority depends on appropriations. Don't count on money that hasn't been appropriated.

updates.title: Marines order Epirus's vehicle-mounted microwave weapon
updates.body: A counter-swarm microwave system on vehicles, the successor to ExDECS.
updates.why: Directed energy has moved from demos to orders.

updates.title: Israel's Iron Beam laser still not fully operational eight months after delivery
updates.body: It was tested with Iron Dome in June, drawing on lessons from the 2026 Iran war. The force reportedly wants more than a dozen batteries.
updates.why: Lasers work, but fielding at scale is slow. There is an opening for power, cooling and integration suppliers.

updates.title: Hadrian raises $1.37B at $7.87B for automated factories
updates.body: Anchored by JPMorgan's strategic fund, with Valor, Baillie Gifford, Founders Fund, a16z and 1789 Capital.
updates.why: Factory automation for the supply base is now a venture category, not just a cost center.

updates.title: Blue Water Autonomy wins a spot on the Navy's $40M deep-ocean mapping contract
updates.body: Long-endurance autonomous ships to survey the Indian and Pacific oceans.
updates.why: Survey work is an early way for autonomous-ship makers to earn revenue while combat programs are contested.

updates.title: Palantir Q2'26: revenue +93% to $1.935B; US commercial +149%
updates.body: US government $809M (+90%), US commercial $764M (+149%), Rule of 40 score 155. FY26 guidance raised to $8.150–8.158B.
updates.why: Commercial revenue is about to overtake US government revenue, which spreads the defense leader's risk.

updates.title: Air Force could choose up to six vendors for CCA Increment 2
updates.body: Nine vendors are in concept refinement and a pool of 20+ may compete. The Air Force is revisiting production goals 'with an eye on scale'.
updates.why: The second round of the biggest autonomous aircraft program is still open.

updates.title: Primes post record backlogs: Lockheed $230B, RTX $289B; guidance raised
updates.body: Lockheed's Q2 sales rose 11% to $20.1B, Missiles & Fire Control +19% (PAC-3, THAAD, PrSM), helped by a $35B THAAD multiyear. Northrop also hit a record.
updates.why: Missile defense and munitions are a boom for incumbents too. New entrants are adding to the market, not replacing them.

updates.title: Karman Space & Defense buys Walker Precision Engineering ($93M), its largest deal yet
updates.body: Karman, up ~200% since its IPO, keeps rolling up niche suppliers. It also agreed to buy Seemann Composites and MSC for $220M.
updates.why: Public newcomers are consolidating the supplier base, a path to exit for component startups.

updates.title: Neros wins a $500M Army IDIQ for Archer FPV drones
updates.body: Under the Purpose Built Attritable Systems program. Output reached about 1,200 drones a week by August.
updates.why: FPV drones are a program of record; the Ukraine model has become US doctrine.

updates.title: Blue Water Autonomy and Saildrone sue the Navy over the MUSV rejection
updates.body: A protest over the Medium Unmanned Surface Vessel selection.
updates.why: New entrants are using the courts against legacy-style procurement. Expect more.

updates.title: Helsing raises at about an $18B valuation
updates.body: Reports put the round at $1.2–1.8B. Its HX-2 strike drone is in Ukrainian service, alongside a €1.46B drone contract.
updates.why: Europe's answer to Palantir plus Anduril is now a top-three private defense company.

updates.title: Quantum Systems signs a €1B Series D at about €7B
updates.body: Co-led by Blackstone, Noteus, Airbus and Advent.
updates.why: Airbus investing signals European incumbents are buying into drone makers.

updates.title: China adds MP Materials and USA Rare Earth to its export-control list
updates.body: Effective immediately, Chinese exports of dual-use items to both companies are banned.
updates.why: Beijing is targeting the US effort to build its own rare-earth supply chain. Heavy rare earths are the pressure point.

updates.title: AUKUS partners test drone-swarming tactics
updates.body: Australian, US and UK soldiers trialled swarms under AUKUS Pillar II.
updates.why: Allied autonomy standards are forming. Firms that can interoperate across the three nations gain.

updates.title: Japan launches a Rapid Interceptor Drone Acquisition Program modelled on Ukraine
updates.body: Systems are to be selected for trials within about three months.
updates.why: Interceptor drones are going global. Asian buyers are open to foreign vendors.

updates.title: CSIS: 'Why software, not drones, will decide the next war'
updates.body: After a 5 June presidential memorandum on autonomy, CSIS argues that AI kill chains, the software that fuses sensors, picks targets and times strikes, are themselves autonomous weapons.
updates.why: Policy definitions will decide who must certify what. That is a compliance market and a moat.

updates.title: Air Force orders CCA production from General Atomics and Anduril
updates.body: The first combat jet built by a defense startup goes into production.
updates.why: Proves the build-before-the-contract model on the hardest product category.

updates.title: SpaceX wins $6.45B across two Golden Dome and space-communications awards
updates.body: $4.16B for SB-AMTI (tracking moving air targets from space) and $2.29B for the Space Data Network backbone, built on MILNET/Starshield, with an operational prototype due by end-2027.
updates.why: One company now holds the military's space backbone, a concentration risk and a platform others will build on.

updates.title: Castelion signs a first-of-its-kind production deal for the Blackbeard hypersonic missile
updates.body: Its Project Ranger site in New Mexico will make at least 500 a year once testing is complete. The company was later valued at about $13B after an $800M raise.
updates.why: Low-cost hypersonics built like consumer hardware challenges the primes' strike franchise.

updates.title: CDAO raises Scale AI's Pentagon deal to $500M
updates.body: Up from $100M in 2025. Covers data labeling and decision support for military AI.
updates.why: The data and evaluation layer under military AI is its own large market.

updates.title: Anduril raises $5B Series H at $61B
updates.body: Its valuation doubled in 11 months. Talks were reported near $100B by July.
updates.why: Private capital can now fund factories, once the primes' moat.

updates.title: Shield AI's Hivemind to run Taiwan's Thunder Tiger sea drones
updates.body: AI autonomy for a coastal-denial network of unmanned surface vessels.
updates.why: US autonomy software combined with allied hardware is a repeatable export model.

updates.title: CBO: Golden Dome could cost $1.2T over 20 years; DoW estimate $185B to 2035
updates.body: Independent estimates range from $175B (White House) to $3.6T (AEI) depending on the design.
updates.why: A huge, contested budget line. Its political survival will shape space and missile-defense startups.

updates.title: FY27 request: $54.6B for DAWG and $53.6B for Drone Dominance
updates.body: DAWG rises from $225M. The drone effort includes $39.2B for autonomous systems procurement and domestic production plus $14.4B for counter-unmanned systems.
updates.why: The biggest budget shift toward autonomy ever. Follow it through Congress.

updates.title: PitchBook: defense-tech VC hits $69.5B over the trailing 12 months
updates.body: Q1 set a record at $19.8B across 262 deals; Q2 brought $16.4B across 249. Autonomy took 42.1% of Q2. Eleven public listings reopened exits.
updates.why: Money concentrates in mega-rounds and seed; mid-stage is hard.

updates.title: Space Force picks 12 firms, including SpaceX, Anduril, Lockheed and True Anomaly, for space-based interceptor prototypes
updates.body: Awards total up to $3.2B, with a demonstration due by 2028.
updates.why: Missile defense, once the primes' preserve, now includes new entrants.

updates.title: Ukraine to field 25,000 ground robots for frontline logistics
updates.body: About 280 companies make 550+ ground-vehicle models, running 10,000+ logistics missions a month.
updates.why: The clearest demand signal yet for ground autonomy, years ahead of the US.

updates.title: DoD components face an 'aggressive' timeline to move onto Maven Smart System
updates.body: Deputy Secretary Feinberg pushed Maven toward a department-wide program of record.
updates.why: How a vendor becomes the standard; once every command runs on Maven, replacing it is very hard.

updates.title: Germany and Ukraine sign a €4B package that includes joint drone production
updates.body: Part of Europe's push to scale autonomous-systems manufacturing.
updates.why: Ukrainian know-how plus European money is becoming a production base that will compete with US firms.

updates.title: Saronic raises $1.75B Series D at $9.25B
updates.body: For autonomous surface vessels and shipyard capacity.
updates.why: Naval autonomy is the next large hardware market.

updates.title: RAND: crosscutting insights for the drone-dominance push
updates.body: Large numbers of attritable, adaptable unmanned systems now cost orders of magnitude less than traditional platforms.
updates.why: Research support for the cheap-mass thesis.

updates.title: Shield AI raises $1.5B Series G at $12.7B
updates.body: Led by Advent and co-led by JPMorgan; Blackstone added $500M of preferred equity.
updates.why: AI pilot software is valued as its own layer, separate from airframes.

updates.title: Anduril and Palantir reported to be leading Golden Dome's software layer
updates.body: Teamed with SpaceX for parts of the constellation; they lead the software that links sensors to interceptors.
updates.why: The command core of the decade's largest program went to newcomers.

updates.title: PLA demonstrates the 'Atlas' swarm: one vehicle launches 96 drones; claims of 200 per operator
updates.body: The drones fly an autonomous anti-jamming path-planning algorithm tested under electromagnetic interference.
updates.why: The pacing threat for US swarm and counter-swarm programs. It drives requirements.

updates.title: Drone Dominance Gauntlet I: 25 vendors compete, 11 selected
updates.body: Held at Fort Benning. About 100 operators flew each system after two hours of training.
updates.why: Easy to learn and cheap to buy beat exotic performance.

updates.title: First known microwave kill of a jam-proof fiber-optic drone
updates.body: Epirus Leonidas disabled a fiber-optic-guided drone in a live-fire demo.
updates.why: Fiber-optic drones made jamming obsolete in parts of Ukraine; microwave weapons and interceptors are the answer.

updates.title: Hanwha Defense USA and HavocAI agree to co-develop 200-ft autonomous surface vessels
updates.body: Korean shipbuilding paired with US collaborative-autonomy software. HavocAI later advanced to Navy MUSV at-sea testing.
updates.why: Foreign shipyards plus US autonomy could relieve the Navy's capacity crunch.

ideas.what: Tracks inventory, firmware, battery health, losses and operator training for thousands of drones from many vendors.
ideas.why: Drone Dominance buys from 11+ vendors and nobody manages the mixed fleet. At 200k units, logistics is the bottleneck.
ideas.wedge: One brigade's FPV fleet through a SBIR or CSO.

ideas.what: Sensor fusion and attribution software (RF, radar, acoustic, camera) for bases, data centers, stadiums, prisons and utilities.
ideas.why: $14.4B FY27 counter-UAS line plus the base-defense pilot. Commercial sites legally can only detect and report drones, so software is what they buy.
ideas.wedge: Commercial sites first, then DoD installations.

ideas.t: Synthetic data and test & evaluation for autonomy
ideas.what: Simulation and synthetic sensor data to train and certify autonomy when GPS is denied and radios are jammed.
ideas.why: New autonomy policy (the June 2026 memo, CSIS definitions) means systems need verification evidence, and the new command gets test powers.
ideas.wedge: Per-campaign service for startups going into gauntlets.

ideas.what: Maps every part to its country of origin, flags NDAA, Blue UAS and the 2027 magnet ban, and finds compliant suppliers.
ideas.why: The 1 Jan 2027 magnet ban and China's 10 Nov deadline hit hundreds of hardware vendors at once.
ideas.wedge: SaaS for drone and munitions startups. Fastest path to revenue.

ideas.t: GPS-denied navigation module ('Intel Inside' for drones)
ideas.what: A small vision, inertial and terminal-guidance board any airframe maker can integrate; later, quantum-ready.
ideas.why: Jamming is everywhere; most vendors can't build autonomy in-house. As airframes become commodities, the margin sits in components like this.

ideas.t: Contract intelligence and capture agent for small vendors
ideas.what: An LLM agent that watches SAM.gov, DIU, OTA consortia, budget documents and portfolio acquisition executives, matches openings to a product, and drafts responses.
ideas.why: Thousands of new vendors are navigating DAWG and the new acquisition rules; turning valuations into orders is the stated test.

ideas.what: Motors using ferrite or reluctance designs, or recycled magnets, for small drones and actuators.
ideas.why: China controls heavy rare earths. A compliant motor is a chokepoint product every drone maker needs.
ideas.wedge: Supply Taiwan's non-Chinese drone chain and US gauntlet vendors.

ideas.what: An autonomous interceptor under $5k for Shahed-class and FPV drones.
ideas.why: Ukraine proved the concept, and Japan, the Gulf and US bases are buying. The cost-exchange crisis is acute.
ideas.wedge: Partner with a Ukrainian team for combat data.

ideas.t: Tactical power and thermal systems for directed energy
ideas.what: Batteries, power conditioning and cooling packs that let lasers and microwave weapons fire continuously on vehicles.
ideas.why: Laser production has started (AeroVironment E-HEL) but fielding is slow (Iron Beam); power and cooling are the constraint.
ideas.wedge: Sell to laser integrators as a subsystem.

ideas.what: Licenses combat-proven Ukrainian designs (ground robots, interceptors, software) and handles compliance and US or EU production.
ideas.why: About 300 Ukrainian ground-drone firms and 500 FPV makers are looking for export routes; Brave1 is certifying exports.
ideas.wedge: Start with ground robots for logistics.

ideas.what: Low-probability-of-intercept mesh radios that keep swarms coordinated under jamming.
ideas.why: Autonomy at scale needs links that survive. Fiber works for one drone, not a swarm.
ideas.wedge: Deep tech that both Lattice and Maven ecosystems would buy.
